_comment: Campaign 01: the within-arm spread, measured. Predictions were registered
in advance in local-lab/CAMPAIGN-01-PREDICTIONS-2026-08-02.md; do not run
this without reading them, because a prediction written after a result is
not a prediction.
Ten runs, three arms. baseline and poison-noop differ by exactly one line:
the poison arm is not a different experiment, it is the same experiment
with the cause removed. If it passes, the oracle is being satisfied by a
file this run did not write, and every result the harness has ever
produced is void.
Replicate suffixes -r1..-rN are what tools/probe/compare.py groups on.
No arm here is judged by coverage: coverage needs TTD, TTD needs an
elevated window, and this manifest is built to run unattended without one.
PREDICTIONS, REGISTERED IN ADVANCE. The commit that adds this file is the
timestamp, and it precedes the first launch. refute.py R03 refuses a
finding whose predictions were written after its results, and it is right
to: on 2026-07-31 five predictions came back MATCH on a law that was
wrong, and they were true under the rival law too.
P1  poison-noop reports FAIL 3/3, on the fileAppears arm.
FALSIFIED BY: any poison-noop PASS. That would mean the oracle is
satisfied by a file the run did not write -- a scratch tree that
inherited data/Memory/baseline.txt, or a teardown that left the
previous tree standing. Either voids every result this harness has
ever produced, not just this campaign's.
P2  baseline reports PASS 4/4.
FALSIFIED BY: any FAIL. A mixed baseline means the instrument is
unreliable at the launch itself and nothing can be compared yet.
P3  Lose prevents the console command after it from running:
lose_after.txt does NOT appear, lose_before.txt does, and the lose arm
reports FAIL for a different reason than the poison arm does.
REASONING: Lose is a mission-outcome command; if it transitions the
game out of the level, the console queue is unlikely to survive it.
FALSIFIED BY: lose_after.txt appearing at >= 1024 bytes.
SCOPE: this is about the console queue, NOT about what Lose does to
life, shields, the augment chain or the death path. None of those are
measured here.
P4  baseline lifetime spread (max - min) is under 10 s.
This is the number the campaign exists to produce: compare.py will not
call any cross-arm difference real unless it exceeds this.
FALSIFIED BY: a spread of 10 s or more, which would mean short-lifetime
probes are useless as instruments.

probes.name: baseline-r1
probes.note: Control. Echo, MemStats, Quit -- the console path proven on 2026-08-02.

probes.name: baseline-r2
probes.note: Identical to baseline-r1. The point is that it is identical.

probes.name: poison-noop-r1
probes.note: POISON. Same launch, same oracle, MemStats line removed. Must FAIL. A PASS here means the oracle is reading a file this run did not write.

probes.name: lose-r1
probes.note: Does a console command after Lose still run? Prediction P3 says no. Both MemStats outputs are collected so 'Lose stopped the queue' and 'MemStats never ran at all' can be told apart.
